about: Every utterance in Pet Island that needs synthesizing. Per docs/pet-island-voice.md §5.1.
This is a RUNNING file: no spoken line may be added to the island without an entry here.
Text is the TARGET wording — i.e. after the splice law of voice.md §3. Where the shipped
code still differs, the entry carries "port": the item that brings the code into line.
A few lines are TEMPLATES and say so by carrying a slot in their text: {n} is a number and
{one|many} is the noun either way. Such an entry also carries "ref", naming the generated
family the slot is filled from — same field, same meaning as on a slot line of its own, and
the family's character must match the line's or the splice is illegal (§3). The template is
written here in full so the wording can be audited as a sentence; the cut is in the note.
The 2D game (src/words2d, v0/junos-words.html) is NOT covered here. It is frozen and its
speech must stay identical to v0, including the spoken child's name at v0:742. The splice

voices.fred: Warm, playful, slower. The island's host. Never speaks a dynamic name.
voices.teacher: One clear British voice, never varies. Owns every challenge word and every pet name — consistency is part of the listening task.
voices.owl: Measured, warm. Not used this phase.
voices.dad: Parent recordings from the sound booth. Phoneme clips and school-list imports.

laws: No character speaks a dynamic name mid-sentence. The child's name is print only; spoken address is 'friend'.
A slotted template and its inserts share one voice. Cross-voice splices are forbidden.
A pet's name is always the teacher's, never a character's — so a name is a line of its own, chained between character lines rather than spliced into one.

generated.source: build-time name table, one entry per {setId, speciesId}
generated.note: Fixed per variant and identical on every island (brief §5, voice.md §2). Graded by set: set 1 at band 1, climbing. Audited before bake; a rejected name is replaced at authoring time, never dropped.
Repeat-on-tap plays the same clip at rate 0.6; grapheme-by-grapheme help plays at 0.9 (src/challenges/build.ts:83,96).

The album pop-out's speak button reads the friend's name and THEN its species, chained on the name's end rather than spoken over it (speak() cancels speech, v0:749). Two clips, never one splice: a name.* clip followed by a species.* clip, per the law that a name is a line of its own. Two of the twenty-four are judgement rather than transcription — 'animal-polar' is 'Polar Bear' and 'animal-hog' is 'Wild Boar', because 'animal-pig' is also in the pack. Same words as printed on the card, so what they hear is what they are reading.

generated.source: spoken numerals, one clip per number
generated.note: FRED's numerals, not the teacher's, because they are spliced into Fred's own sentences — voice.md §3 requires the slot parts and their inserts to share one voice, so the teacher counting inside Fred's line would be exactly the cross-voice splice the law forbids. They are not challenge material either: these are Fred telling the child how many, so the one-voice rule for taught words (§1) does not claim them. Twenty covers every count the corridor can ask for in ordinary play, but the count is unbounded in principle — it is however far past the wall they have walked — and a number with no clip falls back to Web Speech like any other missing line (§6).

lines.text: I'm Fred. It's just me on this little rock.
It's ever so quiet out here.
Eggs come from far across the sea… and they only hatch for someone who reads to them.
Will you read to it, friend?

lines.note: Beat 7 is now three chained lines, not one. Fred, then the teacher announcing the name, then Fred again — a name is never in a character's mouth.
Plays the pet's clip from the name table.

lines.text: Home at last! It was coming home all along.
lines.was: You found its name! [PETNAME] has arrived.

lines.text: Every new friend needs somewhere to live… can you find us some land?
lines.was: Every friend you read home needs somewhere to live… can you count us up some land?

lines.note: Follows a name. clip. Replaces '[PETNAME] has arrived!'
Follows a name. clip. Replaces '[PETNAME] is here!'

lines.text: You have found some land for your friends!
Let's read with the egg — {n} more {friend|friends} will fill it up!
lines.was: Let's read with the egg to get some more friends!
lines.note: A TEMPLATE, and the count is spliced at speak time. JT-019 — Joe: "we get fred to tell her how many she needs to restore balance." The number is a fact about their island at the moment Fred opens his mouth, so there is no whole line to bake: it is cut either side of the numeral, "Let's read with the egg —" | count.n | "more friend(s) will fill it up!". The seam is the em dash, which is a pause he takes anyway (§3 asks for seams on natural boundaries), and the splice is legal because Fred's numerals go into Fred's own sentence — one larynx throughout, as "You found… Bimo!" is one larynx throughout. The tail bakes TWICE, once each way: "1 more friends will fill it up" is a sentence a child learning to read must never be shown, which is why the template spells both forms rather than bolting on an s.

lines.text: They need homes! {n} more {tile|tiles} will do it.
lines.note: The mirror, counted in tiles, and spliced the same way for the same reason (JT-019 — Joe: "we get fred to tell her how many she needs to restore balance."). Cut "They need homes!" | count.n | "more tile(s) will do it.", the seam falling after the opening exclamation, and the tail baked both ways. Fred throughout, so nothing crosses a voice.

lines.text: Ooh, my legs have gone all wriggly! Let's jump up and have a run about — then come back, your island will be right here.
lines.note: Fired when three pages in a row are mashed (3+ wrongs each). Warmer and slower than the other two governor lines — an invitation to play, not a note about the work. FRED owns the need for the break, never the child: brief §19 forbids shame, and a line about their answers is a scoreboard however kindly it is read. Suggestion only — nothing is locked, nothing expires, and they can carry straight on.

lines.text: You are doing really well! Would you like some trickier questions? They will get you eggs and tiles faster.
lines.note: Run B's UNIVERSAL offer line, verbatim from docs/pet-island-runA.md:230-232 — one wording for every path, so the island never sounds as though it has an opinion about which of them they are worse at. Spoken and printed together, because the panel's two buttons are unreadable as a choice if the question is only heard. Fired at a completion high, at most once a session island-wide, and only after the ceremony has released the exits. No whole-line variants: 'trickier' is the word, not 'harder', and the reward clause stays attached — it is the half a five-year-old is actually weighing.

lines.text: Would you like to do some taking away?
lines.note: The other half of Run B's offer, verbatim from docs/pet-island-runA.md:234-235. Short and unadorned on purpose: a whole new kind of maths is its own news, and a sentence selling it would make the honest answer 'no' harder to give. It outranks the trickier offer when both are due (harness.ts:818-842). Fred asks; the minus sign itself is introduced by the pop on their first take-away, not by an explanation.
